title: helm(redwood-private): tighten values schema, improve templating, and stabilize init hooks for upgrade/rollback
author: Ayesha Patel
description:
Context: private deployments rely on the redwood-private Helm chart for on-prem/VPC installs. We've seen a few upgrade/rollback incidents where init hooks (migration jobs and CRD priming) either ran twice or failed to rollback cleanly when chart values had unexpected shapes. This PR tightens the chart values schema, makes templating more defensive, and refactors the init hook jobs to be idempotent and better scoped for upgrades/rollbacks.

What changed (high level):
- Add a strict values.schema.json for charts/redwood-private so Helm can validate user values at install/upgrade time; schema includes typed fields for routing, storage, k8sResources, and initJobs.
- Harden templating around optional fields: use defaulting helpers and explicit nil-checks in _helpers.tpl to avoid rendering invalid k8s manifests when values are omitted.
- Refactor init hooks into two separate Jobs: init-db-migrations and init-crd-primer. Each job has an anchor helper that ensures a single successful run is recorded using a ConfigMap-based lock with a TTL label to allow safe re-runs during rollbacks.
- Add a pre-upgrade check hook that validates compatibility of the incoming values against the schema and will abort upgrade with a readable failure message when incompatible.
- Add Chart tests and a small upgrade/rollback e2e harness for the installer's CI pipeline to exercise the hooks during a simulated upgrade with and without values shape changes.

Why:
- Prevents common support escalations where malformed values lead to partial upgrades or broken rollbacks.
- Makes the chart safer for self-serve customers and for Dedicated/Private installations where operators rely on Helm upgrades.

Checklist (intent-to-merge):
- [x] values.schema.json added and validated against sample values
- [x] Templates updated with helper defaults and nil guards
- [x] Init hooks split and made idempotent using configmap locks
- [x] Pre-upgrade compatibility check implemented
- [x] Unit tests for template rendering added
- [x] CI chart-tests and e2e harness wired into redwood/ci/charts-pipeline

Commits summary: ["ref(chart): add values.schema.json and update Chart.yaml", "fix(chart): defensive helpers for optional values and defaults", "feat(hooks): split init jobs and add configmap lock helper", "test(chart): add chart-test cases for upgrade/rollback scenarios", "ci: add e2e harness for private chart upgrade testing", "docs(helm): document schema and upgrade behavior"]

Files changed (high level):
- charts/redwood-private/values.schema.json  (new schema, ~400 lines)
- charts/redwood-private/values.yaml (default values tightened)
- charts/redwood-private/templates/_helpers.tpl (defaults, lock helpers)
- charts/redwood-private/templates/init-db-migration-job.yaml (new)
- charts/redwood-private/templates/init-crd-primer-job.yaml (new)
- charts/redwood-private/templates/pre-upgrade-check-hook.yaml (new)
- charts/redwood-private/templates/NOTES.txt (docs update)
- charts/redwood-private/Chart.yaml (version bump)
- redwood-private-installer/helm/README.md (docs on upgrade safeguards)

Testing and CI:
- CI initially reported a flaky chart-test in the GKE job; the migration job timing was non-deterministic in the simulator. Fixed by adding exponential backoff and a readiness probe in the job container image, then re-running CI. Final status: all checks passed on second run (helm lint, kubeval, chart-test upgrade/rollback scenarios, installer e2e harness).

Migration notes for operators:
- If you rely on a custom values file, run `helm upgrade --dry-run --values your-values.yaml` with Helm v3.12+ (or use the pre-upgrade-check-hook) to validate shapes against the schema before applying.
- The configmap lock records successful init runs under key: redwood-private-init-locks/<hook-name>. Locks include a ttl label so a rollback+reinstall will not get stuck indefinitely.

Release notes: "Helm chart: redwood-private -- add strict values schema, more defensive templating, and idempotent init hooks to improve upgrade and rollback reliability."

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Overall LGTM. A couple of nits on helper naming and one comment about the TTL semantics on the configmap lock (see inline).
Ayesha Patel: Thanks — renamed helpers to chart_default_* and adjusted configmap ttl to match our 72h rollback window. Added a comment in the helper template explaining the semantics.
Maria Gonzalez: Can we avoid using an exec-based readiness probe in the job container for tests? It made the simulator flaky. Suggest switching to an HTTP /healthz probe in the test image.
Ayesha Patel: Switched test images to expose /healthz and updated chart-tests to use HTTP probes. Re-ran CI and the GKE job stabilized.
Ethan Zhou: Please add a short note to installer README about validating values with `helm template` + kubeval pre-upgrade. Also reformat the NOTES.txt to include explicit rollback steps.
Ayesha Patel: Added the README snippet and expanded NOTES.txt with rollback steps and troubleshooting tips.

notes_for_release_manager: Recommend backport to release/* for private customers using the 1.12.x line. No behavioral breaking changes expected; schema validation may surface malformed values earlier so coordinate with support to warn active customers.
testing_instructions: Run `helm lint` and `helm template --values samples/private-sample.yaml` to validate rendering. Use chart-tests: `./redwood-helm-charts/tests/chart-tests/upgrade-rollback.sh charts/redwood-private samples/private-sample.yaml` to exercise upgrade+rollback hooks in a test cluster.
notes: This PR is focused on installer/helm UX for Private deployments. It does not change runtime code or model-serving logic. Follow-up work: add a migration plan doc for customers with large DBs (ENG-8002).
